title: must / mustn't / have to / don't have to
grammarTitle: must / mustn't / have to / don't have to
grammarNote: Эти модальные глаголы используются для выражения ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬСТВА и ЗАПРЕТА. Ключевое различие: "must" — говорящий сам считает это необходимым (личное убеждение или авторитет). "Have to" — обязательство исходит из ВНЕШНИХ правил (закон, расписание, начальник). "Mustn't" — ЗАПРЕЩЕНО. "Don't have to" — НЕ ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО (но можно).

grammarTable.subject: must
grammarTable.example: "I must study harder." (I feel this is necessary) / "You must attend 80%." (rule I enforce)

grammarTable.subject: have to
grammarTable.example: "She has to submit by Friday." (deadline rule) / "Do you have to wear uniform?"

grammarTable.subject: mustn't
grammarTable.example: "You mustn't plagiarise." / "He mustn't be late — it's the final exam."

grammarTable.subject: don't have to
grammarTable.example: "You don't have to buy all the books." / "She doesn't have to attend that session."

grammarTable.subject: must (past)
grammarTable.example: "She had to submit it yesterday." — No past form of must for obligation.

grammarTable.subject: have to (Q)
grammarTable.example: "Do I have to come?" / "Does she have to sign it?" (NOT "Must I have to?")

grammarExtra.title: must vs have to — same meaning, different source

rows.example: "You must call me when you arrive." (I want this / I insist)

rows.form: have to = external rule or fact
rows.example: "You have to show ID at the border." (the rule says so, not me)
"You must/have to attend 80%" — both work, slight difference in tone.
"She had to redo the exam." (must has no past form for obligation)

grammarExtra.title: mustn't vs don't have to — CRITICAL difference!

rows.example: "You mustn't use your phone in exams." = It is forbidden. You cannot do this.
"You don't have to buy the book." = No obligation. You can if you want.
✗ "You mustn't buy the book." (= you are forbidden to!) vs ✅ "You don't have to buy it."

rows.form: Test: Is it forbidden or just optional?
rows.example: FORBIDDEN → mustn't. OPTIONAL (but can do) → don't have to.
"We have to submit by Friday." / "They have to wear ID at all times."
"She has to attend 80% of classes." (third person: has to, not have to!)
"He doesn't have to attend the optional lecture." (no obligation)
"Do we have to sign the form?" / "Does she have to come in person?"
"She had to miss class — she was ill."
"He didn't have to resubmit — the grade was fine."
"You will have to submit the dissertation by June."

rows.form: No past of mustn't for obligation
rows.example: Use "couldn't" or "wasn't allowed to" for past prohibition.

grammarTip:
Четыре модальных глагола — четыре чётких значения:
① must = сильное обязательство (говорящий сам решил) → "I must study."
② have to = обязательство из внешних правил → "She has to attend 80%."
③ mustn't = ЗАПРЕТ (нельзя!) → "You mustn't plagiarise."
④ don't have to = НЕ ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО (можно, но не нужно) → "You don't have to come."

🚨 Главная ловушка: mustn't ≠ don't have to!
"You mustn't come" = Тебе НЕЛЬЗЯ приходить.
"You don't have to come" = Тебе не НУЖНО приходить (но можешь).

💡 Past of must = had to. Нет прошедшей формы must для обязательства!

exercises.text: Students ___ attend 80% of classes. It's the rule.
exercises.hint: External university rule = "must" or "have to". Both work. "Students must attend 80%." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose: mustn't or don't have to?
exercises.text: You ___ plagiarise — it can result in suspension.
exercises.hint: FORBIDDEN action → "mustn't". Plagiarism is not allowed. "You mustn't plagiarise." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose: mustn't or don't have to?
exercises.text: You ___ buy every book on the list — the library has most of them.
exercises.hint: NOT NECESSARY (optional) → "don't have to". You can buy them if you want, but it's not required. ✅

exercises.text: She ___ (must / submit) her essay yesterday — the deadline was firm.
exercises.hint: Past form of "must" for obligation = "had to". "She had to submit her essay." ✅

exercises.instruction: Form the correct question with "have to".
exercises.text: "___ students ___ show ID at the entrance?"
exercises.hint: "have to" question: Do/Does + subject + have to + base verb. "Do students HAVE TO show ID?" ✅

exercises.text: "You mustn't come" means you are not obliged to come.
exercises.hint: "mustn't" = PROHIBITED. "You mustn't come" = You are NOT ALLOWED to come. To say "not obliged": "You don't have to come." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form of "have to" (3rd person).
exercises.text: She ___ provide documentation if she misses class.
exercises.hint: "she/he/it" → "has to" (not "have to"). "She HAS TO provide documentation." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which sentence means "it is not necessary"?
exercises.text: Choose the sentence that means "it is optional".
opts: "You don't have to memorise every rule."
exercises.correct: "You don't have to memorise every rule."
exercises.hint: "don't have to" = no obligation, optional. The handbook is available online — no need to memorise everything. ✅

exercises.instruction: Complete with "must", "mustn't", "have to", or "don't have to".
exercises.text: I ___ use my phone during the exam — it's strictly forbidden.
exercises.hint: "mustn't" = prohibited/forbidden. Using a phone in an exam is NOT allowed. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ submit it today — the deadline is next week."
exercises.hint: No obligation (it's not needed today) → "doesn't have to". "She DOESN'T HAVE TO submit it today." ✅

exercises.text: "Students ___ submit their dissertation by June next year."
exercises.hint: Future obligation: "will have to" (not "will must" — "must" has no infinitive!). ✅

exercises.text: "Must" and "have to" always have exactly the same meaning.
exercises.hint: "must" = speaker's own conviction. "have to" = external rule. Similar, but different source of authority. Both express obligation, but the tone is different.

questions.hint: External rule (not from the speaker personally) → "have to". "You HAVE TO attend 80%." ✅

questions.text: "You ___ use AI to write your essay." (it is forbidden)
questions.hint: FORBIDDEN → "mustn't". "You MUSTN'T use AI." = Not allowed. ✅

questions.text: "You ___ buy all the books." (it is not necessary but you can)
questions.hint: No obligation → "don't have to". Not forbidden — just not required. ✅
Past of "must" = "had to". "He HAD TO notify the department." ✅

questions.text: "She ___ submit a medical certificate." (3rd person, external rule)
questions.hint: "she" → "has to" (not "have to"!). "She HAS TO submit a certificate." ✅

questions.text: "You mustn't come" = "You don't have to come" — they mean the same.
questions.hint: "mustn't" = forbidden (not allowed). "don't have to" = not necessary (optional). Completely different!

questions.text: "___ I have to sign this form?" (question)
questions.hint: "have to" question: Do/Does + subject + have to? "Do I HAVE TO sign?" ✅ (not "Must I have to?")

questions.text: "I ___ call her immediately — something might be wrong." (my conviction)
questions.hint: "must" = the speaker's own strong conviction. "I MUST call her." = I feel this is necessary. ✅
Future obligation: "will have to". "Students WILL HAVE TO attend." ✅ ("will must" doesn't exist)

questions.text: "She ___ come to the optional workshop." (it's not required)
questions.hint: No obligation (optional) → "doesn't have to". "She DOESN'T HAVE TO come." ✅
Past "don't have to" = "didn't have to". "They didn't have to submit online." ✅

questions.text: "You ___ lie in your application." (prohibited — strong warning)
questions.hint: "mustn't" = strong prohibition. "You MUSTN'T lie." = Not allowed — serious consequences. ✅

questions.text: Which is the correct question for external obligation?
opts: "Do you have to have an ID?"
questions.correct: "Do you have to have an ID?"
questions.hint: "have to" question: "Do you have to...?" ✅ Never "Do you must..." or "Must you have to?"

questions.text: "I didn't have to" is the correct past negative form of "have to".
questions.hint: "didn't have to" = past tense of "don't have to". "I didn't have to go" = it wasn't necessary. ✅

questions.text: "You ___ bring a laptop — they're provided." (it's not necessary)
questions.hint: "don't have to" = no obligation. Not forbidden — they just provide laptops. ✅

questions.text: What is the main difference between "must" and "have to"?
questions.hint: "must" = the speaker feels this is necessary. "have to" = an external rule/fact makes it necessary.
